key_insight: Evaporating capillary bridges between curved solids are governed by a tightly coupled thermo-fluid-adhesion process in which curvature, wettability, and thermal conductivity jointly control mass transfer and adhesion loss.
engineering_relevance: These results inform the design of microgrippers, adhesive joints, and wetting-based handling systems where controllable capillary adhesion and evaporation-driven detachment matter.
method: Computed equilibrium capillary bridge profiles with a level-set method.
Simulated transient evaporation and moving interfaces using a fully coupled ALE framework.
Quantified the roles of substrate curvature, wettability, and thermal conductivity on evaporation, Marangoni circulation, and capillary force evolution.
evidence_signal: The framework was validated against published results for capillary profiles, evaporation rates, and capillary forces, with good agreement reported.
watch_item: The conclusions rely on a coupled numerical model, so real-surface effects such as roughness, contamination, and contact-line hysteresis may alter the predicted adhesion dynamics.
paper_title: Interfacial-Thermo-Fluid-Adhesion Dynamics of Evaporating Capillary Bridges between Curved Surfaces
